seguranca.introducao: The technical measures PathR uses to protect access to your account and the data stored in it—and what you can do on your end.
resumo: Passwords are stored only as Argon2id hashes; the plaintext password is never stored.
Login requires a verified email address, and the account is locked for 15 minutes after 5 incorrect password attempts.
Passkeys and two-factor authentication via an authenticator app are supported.
Session cookies set to `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Strict`, with rolling renewal and "log out of all devices."
Date of birth, resume, photos, and reports encrypted with AES-256-GCM within the app itself, with the key stored outside the database.
Files stored in private storage, delivered only by the server and only to those with permission.
Did you find an error? Please let privacidade@notter.com.br know before sharing it.

senhas.hashA: Passwords are stored only as hashes
senhas.hashB: , an algorithm designed to withstand attacks using graphics cards. Not even the app's operators can see your password.
itens: The password must be at least 10 characters long and include both letters and numbers—this rule is enforced on the server.
After 5 consecutive incorrect passwords, the account is locked for 15 minutes. The lock is temporary to prevent an attack from becoming a way to lock the owner out.
Invalid email addresses and incorrect passwords both receive the same message, so as not to reveal which email addresses are associated with accounts.
Only people who have confirmed their email address can sign up—that way, no one can create an account using someone else's email address.
Confirmation links (valid for 3 days) and new password links (valid for 1 hour) are single-use, and the server stores only their hashes.

fatores.passkeyResto: : You log in using biometrics or the device's PIN. The server stores only the public key, which is tied to the address pathr.notter.com.br—a fake page cannot use it. Add and remove your keys in Settings › Account.
fatores.totpResto: : When this feature is enabled, the login screen also asks for a code from an authentication app. The secret is stored in encrypted form, and the recovery codes are single-use and stored as hashes.
fatores.desafio: Each access key challenge is valid for five minutes and can only be used once.

sessao.cookiesA: The session is stored in cookies
sessao.cookiesD: (We do not process orders placed on other websites.)
itens: The access token is valid for 30 minutes. Renewal uses a second token, which is changed with each use; if a token that has already been changed reappears—a sign that it has been copied—the entire session chain is revoked.
Each request checks with the server to see if the session is still valid. Closed sessions stop working immediately, not just when they expire.
Changing your password logs you out of your other sessions; resetting your password via email logs you out of all of them.
sessao.p1b: Closes all open sessions at once.

itens: Every API endpoint requires a valid session and only returns or modifies records that belong to the logged-in user.
The browser never communicates directly with the database: only the API has the credentials, and the permissions for the database's public roles are revoked across all tables.
Resumes, profile photos, and story photos are stored privately, with no public link. They are only accessible through the server by those with permission.

Date of birth, resume (the file, the extracted text, and what the AI read from it), profile photos, and posts (message, moderator’s response, and photo) are encrypted using AES-256-GCM by the app itself before reaching the database or storage. The key is stored in the server’s secure settings, outside the database: anyone who obtains a copy of the database or the files will see only encrypted text. Each piece of data is tied to the account it belongs to, so copying it to another account won’t unlock it.
Another person's photo will only appear if they are visible in the suggestions or are connected to you.
Moderation areas appear as if they do not exist for any account other than a moderation account.
The data export does not include password hashes, two-factor authentication secrets, or session tokens.

navegador.httpsB: , with HSTS: the browser remembers never to access PathR without encryption.
navegador.csp: It restricts where the website loads scripts, styles, fonts, and connections from, serving as a second line of defense against code injection.
itens: The site cannot be displayed within frames on other pages (X-Frame-Options and frame-ancestors), which prevents clickjacking.
The nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy headers prevent files from being interpreted as something else or embedded by other websites.
The website blocks access to the camera, location, and browser-based payments, which the app does not use.
The interactive API documentation is disabled in production.
Resumes are accepted in PDF, DOCX, ODT, RTF, TXT, and MD formats, up to 10 MB.
Photos (profile and posts) are accepted only in JPG, PNG, or WebP format, up to 5 MB, and the file type is determined by the file size in bytes—not by the filename or what the browser reports.
A screenshot of a report is provided along with a policy that prevents any execution, even if a disguised file were to slip through the checks.
Articles from other websites displayed in the app are filtered on the server against a whitelist before they appear, and the server refuses to retrieve URLs from internal networks.
External links (articles, job postings, courses, AI responses) only become clickable if they are http or https.

limites.p1: Some resources are shared by everyone—the email quota and the artificial intelligence quota. To ensure that no one uses up what belongs to everyone, the server enforces limits:

fichas.detalhe: By IP address.
By IP, in addition to account-based blocking.
And no more than 3 per hour to the same email address.
On the house.
On the house.
On the house.
On the house.

itens: Security events—such as registration, logins, errors, and two-factor authentication—are logged with the date, IP address, and browser. The log never contains passwords, codes, or tokens.
Server errors are logged without any emails, identifiers, or tokens in the message.
A daily automated review checks for errors, reports, and project dependencies, and the moderation team receives a summary via email.
Use a password that you don't use anywhere else, or a password manager.
Register an access key for your device in Settings › Account.
If you suspect that someone has accessed your account, change your password and use “Sign out of all devices.”
Be wary of messages asking for your password: PathR never asks for your password via email. If in doubt, type pathr.notter.com.br directly into your browser instead of clicking on a link.
On shared computers, log out of your account when you're done—this also deletes the offline copy saved in the browser.

vulnerabilidades.p1b: with a description of the problem and the steps to reproduce it. We ask that you do not access, alter, or delete other people’s data, do not disrupt the service, and allow a reasonable amount of time for the issue to be fixed before making it public. PathR does not have a bug bounty program, but we appreciate your reports—and we respond.

limitacoes.notaA: No system is completely secure. PathR is an independent project with no security certifications, and it also depends on the security of the vendors listed in the
limitacoes.notaB: . If a significant incident involving your data occurs, you will be notified, in accordance with the LGPD.

manual.termos: The Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, and Security Policy can be found at pathr.notter.com.br/termos, /privacy, and /security.

intro.p1: PathR creates a study plan based on what you already know and where you want to go, and builds around it by matching you with certificate courses, job opportunities that suit you, languages, and people to study with. Almost everything depends on two things that only you can answer:

inicio.oQueFaz: Your daily dashboard: the "Keep Going" module, the weekly list, the daily sequence, and the consistency chart.
inicio.precisaDe: A roadmap created to show what to do next.

roadmap.oQueFaz: The entire plan, broken down into phases and modules, with the number of hours for each one. Every week, it adjusts based on what you've done (Route Adjustments).
roadmap.precisaDe: Objective and skills met before generating.

trilha.oQueFaz: The module you're in: study materials, a quiz to test what you've learned, and a hands-on activity.

laboratorio.oQueFaz: Code examples walked through line by line, with the values of the variables at each step. Suggest examples based on your roadmap and skill level.

idiomas.oQueFaz: English proficiency levels (A1 to C2), daily practice tailored to your level, and one-tap word translation.

cursos.oQueFaz: Certificate courses for LinkedIn—free at first, depending on how popular the topic is. Select "I already have this" to display it on your profile.
cursos.precisaDe: Goals set in Skills or a target.

vagas.oQueFaz: Real job openings in your area or remote positions—from the ones that suit you best to the ones that suit you least—along with what’s needed for each and the courses to help you get there.
vagas.precisaDe: Selected skills and the city under Settings › Objective.

curriculo.oQueFaz: Submit your resume: The AI reads it and suggests relevant technologies, which you can then review and import.

perfil.oQueFaz: Your profile summary on the app: what you're proficient in, what you're learning, what you want to learn, and your certificates.

amigos.oQueFaz: Invitations, suggestions from people who live nearby or are studying the same subject, and a series of study sessions in pairs—with a card to share at 7, 30, 60, and 90 days.
amigos.precisaDe: An @ (selected during registration; can be edited under Settings › Account).

relatar.oQueFaz: Submit a complaint or suggestion—with a photo if you'd like—and wait for a response from the moderators.

conta.oQueFaz: Name, @, photo, password, passkey, and two-factor authentication.

objetivo.oQueFaz: Where you want to work, the number of hours per week, and the location of the job openings (city and radius in km).

skills.oQueFaz: The technologies included in your plan and the proficiency level for each, ranging from N0 (I want to learn) to N5 (expert).

avisos.oQueFaz: Which emails to receive, whether to appear in friend suggestions, how to export all your data, or how to delete your account.

integracoes.oQueFaz: The status of the services the app uses (AI, job listings, translation, email) — useful when something seems to be down.

regiao.onde: Settings › Objective › Region and Scope of Open Positions
regiao.oQueFazer: Select your city and the maximum number of kilometers you're willing to travel for an in-person job opening.
regiao.depois: Vagas now shows only in-person classes within your radius (remote classes are always shown), and your class schedule follows your time zone.

objetivo.oQueFazer: Choose a predefined destination or describe in free text where you want to go and how many hours per week.
objetivo.depois: The roadmap is designed with that goal in mind, and Job Openings and Courses prioritize what it calls for.

curriculo.oQueFazer: Upload the PDF or DOCX file: The AI will read it and suggest its technologies with an estimated level for you to review.
curriculo.depois: The skills are already filled in during the next step—you just need to check the levels.

skills.titulo: Mark your skills and their levels
skills.oQueFazer: Check the technologies included in your plan and the proficiency level for each one (N0 = I want to learn … N5 = expert).
skills.depois: "Courses" now suggests certificates, "Jobs" compares your tech stack, and "Lab" shows your programming languages.

roadmap.oQueFazer: Create your plan: break it down into phases and modules based on what you already know and your goal, at your own weekly pace.
roadmap.depois: The current track, the weekly list, and your progress appear on the Home page, and the plan updates every week.

idioma.oQueFazer: Take the placement test: it accurately measures your CEFR level (A1 to C2).
idioma.depois: Vagas compares the English you need with your current level, and the daily exercises are tailored to your level.

amigos.oQueFazer: Search for @ or check out suggestions from people who live nearby or are studying the same subject as you.
amigos.depois: By studying on the same day, you create a sequence together—with a card to share at each milestone.

page.historicoNota: The current plan is saved in the history—creating a new one does not delete this one.

notas.a: Vertical timeline: Order comes first; the deadline is on the left.
notas.b: Stages side by side, so you can see the entire scope at a glance.
notas.c: Competency Matrix: Where You Are and How Far the Plan Takes You.

matriz.vazio: This plan does not yet identify skills that match your profile.
matriz.legendaPreenchido: filled = level recorded in your profile
matriz.legendaContorno: contour = the next level this plane reaches

gerar.objetivoPlaceholder: e.g., full-stack Java developer, with a focus on international job openings
gerar.dicaMontando: The AI is writing the levels—it usually takes less than 20 seconds.
gerar.dica: It takes a few seconds: the plan is tailor-made.

etapas.lendo: After reviewing your resume and your skills

chips.entrevistaIngles: I want an interview in English
chips.semIa: Without relying on AI to code
chips.pratico: I prefer hands-on projects to reading

gerar.contextoPlaceholder: e.g., I've been a front-end developer for 3 years, I want to become a full-stack Java developer, and the interview is in June

semSkills.titulo: First, I need to know what you already know
semSkills.descricao: The plan covers the gap between what you know and where you want to go. Send me your resume, and I'll read it and identify the relevant technologies, or you can list your skills yourself.

ajustes.explicacao: The plan is adjusted every week based on the results of the assessments: topics mastered in quizzes are turned into brief review sessions, recurring gaps are given more time, and the schedule adapts to the actual pace of learning.
ajustes.semAjuste: No adjustments are necessary—the plan is consistent with the measurements.
ajustes.erroFallback: I wasn't able to adjust the route.

noticias.descricaoComCidade: Technology events and announcements in{cidade}, and the surrounding area.
noticias.descricaoSemCidade: Add your city to your profile to see events near you — for now, these are from all over.
noticias.erroCalendario: I was unable to generate the calendar file.

euVou.explicacao: Your presence will be visible to others on your card if you allow it in Settings › People.

vazio.comCidade: We haven't found any tech events near you yet. Check back later—the search will run again in a few hours.
vazio.semCidade: Add your city to your profile so the event search knows where to look.

extensao.descricao: The browser extension reads the job posting and fills it out with what PathR already knows about you—including attaching your resume. For anything it doesn’t know, it asks you right then and there, and your answer is saved for future job postings on any website. You’re still in charge of submitting the application.
extensao.comoInstalar: Install the "extensão/" folder in chrome://extensions (Developer Mode → Load unpacked) and paste the key into the small window there.
extensao.copieAgora: Copy it now: this key won't appear again.
